body_ar: وبهذا تعلمون أن حفص الدوري مثلا توفي في القرن الثالث والخاقاني توفي في القرن الرابع، ومكي بن أبي طالب توفي في القرن الخامس، وأهل الأندلس عموما اشتهروا بإتقان هذا العلم ولذلك فإن مكيا كان مجددا فيه ثم جاء بعده أبو عمرو الداني وهو إمام علوم القرآن كلها بلا منازع، ثم بعده تلميذه أبو داود سليمان بن النجيح وهو كذلك خليفة الداني في هذا العلم، فأهل الأندلس اشتهروا بعلوم التجويد وبتفسير القرآن كذلك فمنهم ابن عطية وابن جزي والقرطبي وأبو بكر بن العربي وغيرهم من أئمة أهل التجويد كأبي حيان وابن الفرس المالكي مؤلف كتاب أحكام القرآن، فلهم مؤلفات كثيرة جدا في خدمة القرآن.
body_en: And by this you know that Hafs al-Duri, for example, died in the third century, and al-Khaqani died in the fourth century, and Makki ibn Abi Talib died in the fifth century. The people of al-Andalus in general were renowned for their mastery of this science, and for that reason Makki was a renewer in it. Then after him came Abu Amr al-Dani, who is without dispute the foremost authority in all the sciences of the Qur'an; and after him his student Abu Dawud Sulayman ibn al-Najih, who was likewise al-Dani's successor in this science. The people of al-Andalus were renowned for the sciences of the rules of Qur'anic recitation (tajwīd), and for Qur'anic exegesis (tafsīr) as well — among them Ibn Atiyyah, Ibn Juzayy, al-Qurtubi, Abu Bakr ibn al-Arabi and others — and for others among the leading authorities in tajwid, such as Abu Hayyan and Ibn al-Faras al-Maliki, the author of the book Ahkam al-Qur'an. They have a very great many works in the service of the Qur'an.

flags.context: ثم بعده تلميذه أبو داود سليمان بن النجيح وهو كذلك خليفة الداني في هذا العلم
options: Abu Dawud Sulayman ibn al-Najih (as the source has it)
Abu Dawud Sulayman ibn Abi al-Qasim ibn Najah
flags.note: The student and successor of Abu Amr al-Dani is usually named Sulayman ibn Najah (d. 496 AH). The source here reads ابن النجيح. The form has been kept as given rather than corrected, per house rule 11; the Sheikh's office should say whether this is a transcription slip in the tape or a variant the Sheikh used.

al-Jazariyyah is the versified primer on Qur'anic recitation by Ibn al-Jazari, and 'the author' throughout this series is Ibn al-Jazari. The series title is left transliterated and untranslated. Articles 436-446 are tapes of this one series; their tape numbering in the titles does not run in the same order as the article IDs.
The Sheikh is placing the early authorities of Qur'anic recitation in century order and crediting the Andalusian school; no ruling is given in this excerpt.
